diagnostic_interpretation: Probe1 builds and the 256 raw native observations pass per SDK. Owner comparison stops on the first existing explicit mixed-mode refusal. No native expectation fails.
Green1 passes all eight new groups per SDK before the immutable full regression. This diagnostic source is recorded as a working-tree identity, not claimed as the later clean qualified commit.

native_oracle.method: Fresh pinned local Intel KVM VM/vCPU per case; one initial SREGS write, no intermediate host mode or control rewrites. KVM backing pre-faulted; equal page A/D input bits remove the terminal HLT observation delta. Compare all 16 represented GPRs, DR0..3/6/7, PC/flags, represented segment/control fields and every RAM byte. Existing segment comparisons treat unusable cache fields as opaque; these fixtures use nonnull caches. No complete XSAVE or unspecified machine bank comparison is claimed.
native_oracle.debug_preparation: The CPL0 TF/GD cases first execute an original DR7 read with GD clear to release lazy KVM interception, then set DR7/TF/SS shadow with original guest instructions. Native host debugging is not enabled. CPL3 priority cases fault before executing a debug transfer.
limitations: Only the local pinned Intel P/E cores are measured. Production code uses supplied profiles and does not infer a CPU model from the host.
Native runs are uninterrupted. Physical backing pauses, forged full-bank changes and changed-context policies are software contract tests against uninterrupted software baselines.
Generated observations enter code64 from compatibility16/32 by original far JMP; generated source compiles for host x64. Protected16/32 comparisons are direct original-byte owner executions.

coverage: Four non64 modes, all eight DR encodings, read/write, ignored operand/address/segment/REP prefixes and all Mod encodings; non64 reads expose low32, DR0..3 writes zero the complete high half even when low32 is unchanged, and unaddressed banks retain high bits.

The common debug access owner retains CPL/GD/DE/LOCK and alias priority. DebugAddressWritten reports only a completed DR0..3 write, survives an immediate accepted event, and is not emitted again by event-only resume.

Generated HighC/LLVMC code64 with host-x64 Clang/NeverC at O0/O2 reads all four complete DR addresses after the non64 instruction. Both reads and writes are compared with the same original guest stream.
TF following DR0 writes/reads and DR7 enable/disable observes the updated comparator bank. The local full-address view prevents a high address from aliasing a low32 next-PC match.
Original GD, LOCK, DE alias, real MOV-SS shadow and CPL3 priority compare delivered frames, debug control/address banks and ordinary RAM.

Twenty-four software recovery cases per SDK cover completed TF and uncompleted GD at IDT, first-frame and second-frame backing. Full bank changes reject, accepted bindings stay frozen through changed contexts, and zero-budget resumes neither repeat the addressed write nor charge attempts or completions.

Twenty software admission cases per SDK require every low32 DR address to agree with its supplied full-width view before fetch or control/RAM effects. Correct reads retain full addresses and produce no write receipt.

Regression includes full paged source, legacy source, shared event/native paging plus standalone legacy debug-register software/native matrices, low instruction-boundary and SDK source integration on both SDKs.
boundaries: NeverC remains host/source x64. No 32-bit source target is restored.

This closes the mode-aware debug-register integration, not all non64 state owners. Ports/strings/MPX, legacy returns, task/system selectors, descriptor queries, fast-system entry, call gates and VM86 composition remain separate work.
Cross-line event accessed updates, further machine transitions, software SMM/SGX, unbound asynchronous producers and physical SGX qualification remain open.
Production LLVM remains neverd-llvm-v23.0.0-r6. No final release, pin or LLVM source gitlink change.

oracle_admission_followup.scope: Intel and KVM pre-fault native-oracle admission, with immediate propagation of helper skips; software-only groups remain ungated.
